Extract estimates and standard errors from a data frame or list

Source: R/input-metafor.R, R/methods.R, R/format-print.R
as_bef_data.Rd

bayes_efron_fit() needs a vector of effect estimates and a vector of their standard errors. as_bef_data() extracts the two vectors from a data frame, a list or an escalc object from the metafor package and checks them. The result is a bef_data object, which can be passed to bayes_efron_fit() in place of the two vectors.

Usage

as_bef_data(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_bef_data(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'list'
as_bef_data(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'escalc'
as_bef_data(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
as_bef_data(
  x,
  ...,
  theta_hat = NULL,
  sigma = NULL,
  variance = FALSE,
  site = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'bef_data'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_data'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_data'
format(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'bef_data'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

For as_bef_data(), a data frame, a list, an escalc object from the metafor package or a bef_data object; see Details. For print(), format() and as.data.frame(), a bef_data object.

...

For as_bef_data(), these dots are for future extensions and must be empty. The print() method passes them on to format(); the other methods ignore them.

theta_hat, sigma

For a data frame, the names of the columns that contain the estimates and the standard errors, as character strings. If NULL (the default), the columns are found by name; see Details.

variance

For a data frame, set to TRUE if the column specified in sigma contains variances. Their square roots are then used as the standard errors.

site

For a data frame, an optional character string naming a column of site labels. If NULL (the default), row names that have been set are used as labels.

object

A bef_data object.

use_cli

For format(): if TRUE and the cli package is installed, the first line is in bold; if FALSE, the result is plain text. If NULL (the default), the value of getOption("bayesEfron.use_cli", TRUE) is used.

row.names, optional

Not used; they are arguments of the generic function.

Value

An object of class bef_data, which is a list with the following components.

theta_hat

The estimates.

sigma

The standard errors.

names

The site labels, or NULL if there are none.

source

"list", "data.frame" or "metafor::escalc", depending on the class of x.

Details

The methods differ in where they look for the estimates and the standard errors.

For a list, the elements theta_hat and sigma are used. Site labels are taken from an element names or, if there is none, from the names of theta_hat.

For a data frame, the estimates are the column named theta_hat, yi, estimate, effect or y, and the standard errors are the column named sigma, se, std_error, stderr or sei. If the data frame has more than one of these columns, the first in the list is used. If the data frame has none of the columns for standard errors but a column vi, var or variance, as a metafor data set does, the square roots of that column are used, with a message. Use the arguments theta_hat and sigma to specify columns with other names. For a column of variances with another name, specify it as sigma and set variance = TRUE. If sigma names a column whose name begins with vi or var and variance is not TRUE, a warning is issued, because the name suggests that the column contains variances. Site labels are taken from the column named in site. Without site, the row names are used if they have been set.

For an escalc object, the estimates are the column yi and the standard errors are the square roots of the column vi. Site labels are the study labels given to metafor::escalc() in its argument slab or, without them, row names that have been set.

A bef_data object is checked again and returned.

At least 5 sites are required. An error is thrown if a value is missing, if a standard error is not positive, or if a site label occurs more than once. The site labels are stored in a fitted model: they are shown in its tables and plots, and sites can be selected by their labels.

Functions

  • print(bef_data): Prints the number of sites and the ranges of the estimates and of the standard errors.

  • summary(bef_data): Returns a list with the number of sites K and summaries of theta_hat and sigma.

  • format(bef_data): Returns the lines that print() shows as a character vector.

  • as.data.frame(bef_data): Returns a data frame with one row per site and the columns site, label, estimate and se. If there are no site labels, label is the site number.

See also

bayes_efron_fit(), krw_discrimination

Examples

# A data frame: the columns `yi` and `sei` are found by name.
dat <- as_bef_data(krw_discrimination)
dat
#> <bef_data>
#> Sites: 97
#> Source: data.frame
#> theta_hat: min -0.02254; median 0.01781; max 0.09817
#> sigma: min 0.005344; median 0.01581; max 0.0392

# The same from the variances, with firm IDs as site labels.
as_bef_data(krw_discrimination, sigma = "vi", variance = TRUE, site = "firm_id")
#> <bef_data>
#> Sites: 97
#> Source: data.frame
#> theta_hat: min -0.02254; median 0.01781; max 0.09817
#> sigma: min 0.005344; median 0.01581; max 0.0392
#> Names: 1, 2, 3, ...

# A list.
as_bef_data(list(theta_hat = krw_discrimination$yi, sigma = krw_discrimination$sei))
#> <bef_data>
#> Sites: 97
#> Source: list
#> theta_hat: min -0.02254; median 0.01781; max 0.09817
#> sigma: min 0.005344; median 0.01581; max 0.0392

# The two vectors that bayes_efron_fit() takes.
str(dat[c("theta_hat", "sigma")])
#> List of 2
#>  $ theta_hat: num [1:97] 0.04696 0.022 0.04216 0.00571 0.03408 ...
#>  $ sigma    : num [1:97] 0.0162 0.0153 0.023 0.015 0.0215 ...

# An escalc object from the metafor package.
es <- metafor::escalc(measure = "GEN", yi = yi, vi = vi, data = krw_discrimination)
as_bef_data(es)
#> <bef_data>
#> Sites: 97
#> Source: metafor::escalc
#> theta_hat: min -0.02254; median 0.01781; max 0.09817
#> sigma: min 0.005344; median 0.01581; max 0.0392
